basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the zoning classification and license-transfer requirement in writing with SF Planning Department Current Planning staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting with the planner assigned to the NCT-Valencia district. Ask: (1) whether a 40-seat concept serving beer and wine with limited food and live entertainment until 1 a.m. will be classified as a Bar or a Restaurant under Planning Code § 102; (2) whether a Type 42 or upgraded Type 41 license transferred from another bar inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD will satisfy Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C); and (3) whether the concept as described will need both a CUA for the bar use and a separate CUA or notification for nighttime entertainment, or whether one CUA can cover both. Bring a written concept description, floor plan sketch and the address.

filing_playbook.action: Identify and enter into escrow for an ABC Type 42 license currently held by a bar located inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Engage an ABC license broker to search for available Type 42 licenses held by bars within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD boundaries. Verify with the broker and Planning that the source premises is inside the SUD. Negotiate the purchase price and enter escrow; make the lease at 995 Valencia contingent on ABC approval of the license transfer. Do not file the CUA until you have a license in escrow or a commitment letter, because Planning Code § 249.60 makes the license source a hard requirement.

filing_playbook.action: File the Health Permit to Operate application with SF Department of Public Health Environmental Health Branch.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at least one month before opening with: (1) the SF Business Account Number (BAN); (2) the Location ID (LIN) assigned during plan check; (3) the federal EIN; (4) proof that a certified food safety manager is on staff (ServSafe or equivalent); and (5) the $470 Permit to Operate application fee. The inspector will verify that the kitchen matches the approved plans and the certified manager is identified. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes. No annual license fee is due for 2026–28 for restaurants and bars.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline: 120–300 days is the time to obtain the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per catalog entry, filing to Commission approval), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days, filing to Commission approval), Health permit to operate (14–45 days, application to final inspection and issuance), and Building permit with change of use (14–120 days for plan review, plus construction time). These are run in sequence (CUA first, then POE and building permit in parallel after CUA approval, then health permit after building final), so the total timeline is dominated by the CUA. The 120–300 day range is for approvals; it does not include time to denials, withdrawals or cancellations. Two comparable bar CUAs in the immediate area (2010.0680C and 2019-014253CUA) were withdrawn or cancelled before a Commission vote, one after 155 days and one after 98 days, so those figures are not included in this approval timeline. Cost: $7,153–$24,050 covers CUA filing fee ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost and fee waiver eligibility), POE permit application ($2,708), health permit to operate ($470) and health plan check ($828–$2,500), building permit ($800–$15,000), and sign permit ($300–$1,500). ABC license transfer fees ($1,000–$1,600) and the purchase price of the license itself ($25,000–$75,000 estimated for a Type 42 in SF) are not government fees and are excluded. State and city business registration, tax accounts and staff training total roughly $250–$1,000 and are also excluded as non-entitlement costs. Music licenses (ASCAP, BMI) are annual subscription fees, not one-time government costs. The timeline assumes no appeals, no discretionary review, and a complete application; protests or incomplete plans can add 60–180 days.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St is currently a restaurant (Sarita's Grill & Beer) with an active Type 41 beer-and-wine license issued in November 2023. The zoning pathway reads the concept as a Bar requiring Conditional Use Authorization in the NCT-Valencia district, and as a change of use from Restaurant to Bar. The site sits inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which imposes two critical requirements: (1) any new or relocated Bar must use a liquor license transferred from another Bar already located inside the SUD, and (2) operating conditions under Planning Code § 202.2 plus lighting and signage requirements apply. The block is dense with food and beverage uses—24 registered businesses and 9 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft—and the last decade shows only three dated use decisions within 1,000 ft (too few for an approval rate), with one approved, zero denied, and two withdrawn.
